messages:
maria: heads-up — CI run on main just hit repeated OOMs in the kv cache worker after the kernel-selection change merged earlier today. full job log shows >80% memory retained by slabs even with low traffic. stack excerpt below.
maria: ```
runtime: oom
goroutine 1 [running]:
  kvcache/evict.go:123 handleEvict
  ...
``` 
maria: correlates with seqlen-heavy regression test (long-context perf suite). reverting locally fixes OOMs.
ashwin: thanks, Maria. can you confirm which PR? is it the kernel routing patch (PR #487)?
maria: yes PR #487 landed ~10:12 UTC. I did a quick `git revert` locally and the CI test passes.
ben: hmm. PR #487 changed kernel selection to prefer larger tile kernels for >512 seq. could be interacting with our slab sizing heuristic — larger kernels increase KV cache footprint per batch.
ben: also noticed a change in the batching heuristic in the same rollout: `batch_window_ms` bumped to 15ms in config map. might increase concurrent KV entries.
maria: @ashwin @ben here's a small reproducer I used: run `make perf-longctx` then feed the seqlen-1024 test prompt. memory climbs until OOM in ~25s.
ashwin: can you attach `pmap`/`smem` snapshot at ~15s? and `cat /proc/<pid>/maps | grep kvcache` if possible.
maria: attached snippets in the job output (lines ~3420-3440). kv slabs show many >2MB chunks still referenced.
tia: pinging infra — @deploy-bot did the rollout yesterday show any node config differences? any nodes with different kernel binary or driver versions?
deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T10:05:42Z: rolled main -> prod 3 nodes at 10:12 UTC. No driver changes. configmap `runtime-config` updated: `batch_window_ms: 15` and `kernel_prefer_large_tiles: true`.
ashwin: ok, plan: (1) run bisect between pre-487 and HEAD focusing on kernel selector and batching change, (2) add ephemeral extra logging in evict path to emit slab occupancy and candidate select reasons, (3) try config rollback (batch_window_ms -> 8) on a canary node.
ben: I'll start a local bisect: `git bisect start HEAD v1.2.4 -- tests/perf/longctx`. if it points to kernel selector, we should consider making slab_size proportional to kernel tile size as a quick mitigation.
maria: starting canary with config rollback now on us-west-2-canary-1; will post results in ~12m.
maria: canary looks stable so far — memory plateaued instead of growing. no OOM after 9 mins of longctx load.
ashwin: great. can we gate the rollback as a quick mitigation and keep bisect running? I want to capture perf traces for the failing variant.
tia: approved rollback on canary; if stable for 30m we can promote and open a rollback release.
ben: running `perf record -F99 -p <pid> -- sleep 20` against failing build, will upload flame to the thread when done.
maria: summary/action items: 1) promote batch_window rollback if canary holds (TIA) 2) ashwin to finish bisect and root-cause 3) ben to propose slab sizing change and perf artifact. tagging @eng-runtime leads for triage. :thumbsup:
